title: Architecture Publisher
question: How does Architecture Publisher turn an architecture model into a print edition and an HTML page?
summary: A build validates the model, gives each file in its scope at the pinned revision to the component that claims it, plans the views and lays each out on one grid. It typesets a print edition: the model's overview and one plate per view, each part a card with a strip whose length is in proportion to the size of its files. It also writes one HTML page, which is the author's guide when the model names one; the edition as data, with a reader file for a reader that works from text; and a manifest of their digests. A named reviewer accepts the delivery before it is published.
scope: Architecture Publisher as released at v0.15.0: the publisher's source under src/, its package manifest and the manifests of its vendored supplies.
limits: A component lists only the files under the paths it claims, each file given to its most specific claim; a relation lists only the modules that import or call the other component.
Relations show only imports and process calls in the source, not runtime order; none is drawn for the shared refusal type or the child environment.
The vendored programs, fonts and artwork that the supply manifests list, and the repository's tests, tools, documentation, OpenSpec Changes and CI, are outside the scope.

overview.claim: Meaning, evidence, form and acceptance each have one owner
overview.lead: The publisher draws any repository's architecture from an explicit model, binds every byte of a delivery to its inputs, and publishes only what a named reviewer accepted.

views.title: One build, end to end
views.question: Which parts does one build pass through, from the author's model to a published delivery?
views.summary: The author runs archpub build, and the delivery builder makes plates, the print edition, the page, and the data with its reader file. The reviewer runs compare, accept and verify; the Acceptance and publication stage sets a colophon page beside the delivery and copies only an accepted delivery to the publication root.

views.title: Files at the pinned revision
views.question: How does a build give each file to the component that claims it, and what does the archpub check command report?
views.summary: At the pinned revision, File binding gives each file in the scope to its most specific claim and reads its digest, size and last change; from these the Measured facts check gives each part its size and each file its age band, and the data keeps one row of evidence for each path. The coverage report counts owned, uncovered and excluded files; the re-pin worklist lists what moving the pin changes.

views.title: Where a model comes from
views.question: Which parts bring a model in from LikeC4 or from an earlier version, and which validates every model?
views.summary: The author writes the model; through archpub, the LikeC4 importer parses a LikeC4 workspace and Model migration converts a version 1 or 2 model to version 3. The model loader validates every model as version 3.

views.title: Grid layout
views.question: How does one grid lay out both the plates and the page's diagrams?
views.summary: Rows come from tiers or relations. Placement solves card positions exactly, the Wires part groups relations into buses and corridors, and the channel solver routes each channel; the neatness measure refuses any overlap.

views.title: The print edition
views.question: What turns the planned views into the print edition, and which supplies does it use?
views.summary: The plate composer turns each planned view into one plate and draws each part as one card, with a strip whose length is in proportion to the size of its files. The Print edition part typesets every plate and the overview, which is drawn from what the model states, in one Typst pass; the Supplies part provides the fonts and the icons.

views.title: The page
views.question: How is the page made, and what is checked on the way?
views.summary: The Explainer page part runs Archify and delivers one panel per view, or the author's guide when the model names one. The Guide part clones the repository at the pinned revision to verify every cited range there.
